hyperedges.label: Uaxactún Multi-Project Research Cluster

attributes.description: Multidisciplinary scientific hub founded in 2015 at the Faculty of Arts, Comenius University in Bratislava. Focuses on Maya, Nahua, and broader Mesoamerican cultures. Located at Štúrova 9, within the Department of Comparative Religious Studies. Reports directly to the dean of the Faculty of Arts.
Host institution of the Center for Mesoamerican Studies, Faculty of Arts, Bratislava, Slovakia.

Prof. Milan Kováč PhD. from Comenius University. Lead researcher of long-term multidisciplinary projects at Uaxactún, Guatemala. PI on VEGA 1/0011/13 (Maya hieroglyphic inscriptions) and VEGA 1/0858/17 (Maya Preclassic period synthesis).
Mgr. Jakub Špoták, PhD. Researcher on Project 09I03-03-V04-00243: Function of Tzolk'in Calendar Structures in the Postclassic Maya Codices. Contact email: jakub.spotak@uniba.sk.
Researcher on CU grant 2025: Documentation of rock art motifs from the Kaua Cave in Yucatán, Mexico, using LiDAR. Also authored the Preliminary catalog of rock art in the Kaua Cave (2025).

Uaxactun Regional Archaeological Project overseen by CMS since 2016. One of the most significant European research initiatives in the Maya area. CMS provides funding, technical support, research coordination, and publication work.

Archaeological site in Guatemala, considered a cradle of Mayan civilization. Site of Slovak long-term multidisciplinary research led by Prof. Milan Kováč. Contains pre-Classic and Classic Maya monuments including stelae first recorded by S. G. Morley in 1916.
Legacy web page for papers associated with the PARU Uaxactún project. Page title: Papers.
Legacy web page listing recent investigations under the PARU Uaxactún project.
Legacy web page for archaeological artefacts from the PARU Uaxactún project.
Legacy web page listing archaeological project reports. Subtitle: Archaeological Projects: Uaxactun, Guatemala. Focus on Maya civilization conservation and presentation of Slovak discoveries.

Maya Ritual and Astronomical Complex project. Goal: verify, explain, and preserve a new ritual and astronomical observatory discovered by Slovak research in Uaxactún, Guatemala (100 BC – 150 AD). Includes creating a 3D model, exhibition in Slovakia, collaboration with the Hlohovec observatory, nanotechnology preservation of stucco mask, and physical replica construction.

Project focused on new reading of Maya hieroglyphic inscriptions from Uaxactún, Guatemala. Goals: digital documentation of stelae using modern technology (frottage, night photography, RTI, 3D photogrammetry), updated interpretation by international team, publication of new corpus of hieroglyphic inscriptions. Led by Prof. Milan Kováč. Previous documentation by Graham (1986) contained ~30% errors.

Project aimed at revising the state of knowledge on the Maya Preclassic period. Motto: 'back to the origin of Maya history'. Duration 2016–2020. Led by Prof. Milan Kováč's team. Integrates data from five international projects: El Mirador, Ceibal, San Bartolo, Holmul/Cival, and Uaxactún. Goals include data completion, chronology calibration, architectural/urban typology, writing system database, visual forms database, and synthesis.
Preclassic Maya Potbelly Sculptures in Peten, Guatemala and Their Connection to Ancestor Cult. Researcher: prof. Milan Kováč, PhD. Includes a preliminary database (A1-Database - POTBELLY.pdf).
Function of Tzolk'in Calendar Structures in the Postclassic Maya Codices. Researcher: Mgr. Jakub Špoták, PhD.

Annual conference organized by CMS since 2009 (formerly Autumn Academy of Maya Hieroglyphic Writing). Combines workshops in Maya hieroglyphic decipherment with a scholarly conference. Editions include: 9th BMM (2019, topic: Mesoamerican Worldviews), 8th BMM (2018, topic: Lights and Shadows of Xibalba), 7th BMM (2016, topic: Imago Mundi), 6th BMM (2015, topic: Maya Ritualism), and earlier Academy editions from 2010–2014.

The leading Maya-focused academic gathering in Europe. CMS has been co-organizer since 2014 and formally represented the event in 2020 and 2025. 19th edition held in 2014 in Bratislava with topic: Maya Cosmology: Terrestrial and Celestial Landscapes.
Recurring conference cycle held in both the Czech Republic and Slovakia, where CMS researchers regularly present.

Specialized library overseen by CMS, holding over 10,000 volumes related to pre-Columbian civilizations with focus on Mesoamerica. Includes rare facsimiles, codices, early prints, and the personal archive of Ferdinand Anders. Open to students and visiting researchers.

New ritual and astronomical observatory discovered by Slovak research in Uaxactún, Guatemala. Dates to 100 BC – 150 AD. Features a jaguar god mask on the observatory façade. Described as potentially the oldest and most significant Mayan observatory.

Stelae inscriptions at Uaxactún, among the oldest discovered, first recorded by S. G. Morley in 1916. Previous documentation by Graham (1986) contained ~30% errors. Target of VEGA 1/0011/13 redocumentation project.

Earliest epoch of Maya civilization. Knowledge remains fragmentary compared to Classic and Postclassic periods. Primary focus of VEGA 1/0858/17. International collaborating projects include El Mirador, Ceibal, San Bartolo, Holmul/Cival, and Uaxactún.
Cave in Yucatán, Mexico. Site of rock art documentation project using LiDAR by researcher Fátima del Rosario Tec Pool (CU grant 2025).
Observatory in Hlohovec, Slovakia. Collaborating institution for verifying calculation accuracy and creating graphic models of the Uaxactún astronomical observatory in project APVV-0864-12.
